statements.venue: Press release on federal coal investment
statements.quote: Clean, beautiful, Kentucky coal can be a centerpiece of America’s energy dominance, create good paying jobs, and help us win the race for AI against China.
statements.context: Barr praising a federal investment in Kentucky coal-fired power plants.
statements.reason: About competing with China on AI and energy supply; no catastrophic risk acknowledged.

statements.venue: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing, 'Winning the AI Arms Race Against the Chinese Communist Party'
statements.quote: Because of this, we are on the precipice of losing the AI race,
statements.context: Barr referring to China's construction of new coal-fired power plants, arguing for more US coal power for data centers.
statements.source_label: Roll Call, 14 April 2026 (reporting the January hearing)
statements.reason: Race with China framing only; no catastrophic risk acknowledged.

statements.venue: Remarks to the press, reported by WUKY / Associated Press
statements.quote: Even with competition from Communist China with DeepSeek and AI... and I respect Marc Andreessen when he says this is the Sputnik moment... I think we're ready for this competition,
statements.context: Barr responding to the DeepSeek market shock, saying the US is ready to compete with China on AI.
statements.reason: Competition with China on AI; no catastrophic risk acknowledged.

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing AI development. His own bill (H.R. 5927) would speed up approval of AI data centers and their power supply, but that is not a statement against a safety-motivated slowdown.

pause.note: No statement found for or against a pause on frontier AI development.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on the pace of AI development. As a House member he could not sign the 23 September 2026 senators' letter, and no source seen shows any involvement.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Sponsored H.R. 5927, the Securing Reliable Power for Advanced Technologies Act, which would amend the Defense Production Act to fast-track 'critical artificial intelligence infrastructure' (data centers of at least 50 megawatts and the power plants, transmission and fuel supply serving them); referred to House Financial Services.

grade_reason: Barr has spoken about AI several times since 2025, always as a race with China to be won through energy (especially coal) and data centers, or as a jobs concern; none of these acknowledges catastrophic risk, so the level is D. No statement dismissing catastrophic risk was found, so not F.
notes: IMPORTANT: none of the eight web searches ran; the shared web search budget was already used up, so all eight required searches (superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium, China agreement, 'AI safety', official-site search, Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, 23 September 2026 letter) were refused. This result therefore rests only on pages opened directly and is much weaker than a normal run; it should be rerun when search is available. What was checked directly: (1) titles of all press releases on barr.house.gov from 3 January 2025 to 10 November 2026 (pages 1 to 15 of the press release list): no title concerns AI. Only titles were read, not the body of each release, so a passing AI remark inside a release would have been missed. (2) The campaign site barrforsenate.com home and issues pages: no mention of AI. (3) Congress.gov data for bills he sponsored and co-sponsored, scanned by title only: no bill with 'superintelligence' in the title, and no Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, appeared among the first 250 co-sponsored bills (which covered the 119th Congress portion seen) or the first 100 sponsored bills; the sponsored list has 223 items and the co-sponsored list 1,752, so the scan was not complete for older items, and the reading tool truncated long pages. (4) The two events: Barr is a House member until January 2027, so he was not eligible to sign a senators' letter or co-sponsor a Senate bill; no source seen shows him signing or co-sponsoring either, and I could not open the letter or the bill's co-sponsor list to confirm. Not checked at all: hearing remarks (he chairs a House Financial Services subcommittee and may have spoken about AI in banking there; the committee site refused access), floor speeches, interviews, op-eds and news coverage (Kentucky Lantern, Lexington Herald-Leader and Courier Journal searches were blocked or not reachable; LEX18 and WUKY searches showed nothing linking Barr to AI in the first page of results). No press release for H.R. 5927 was found in the press release titles. The record links to congress.gov for H.R. 3447 and H.R. 1121 were not opened (congress.gov returned 403); the facts came from the official api.congress.gov data. The date for the Chip Security Act is his co-sponsorship date, not the bill's introduction date. No paraphrased statements were left out, because none were found. Searches rerun on 15 November 2026: 10 ran, none refused; 3 new statements. Corrections: Not strictly a correction, but the existing file says no AI statement in his own words was found. There are some (all level D, listed above). The existing file's statement that no press release title concerns AI still holds: the 14 January 2026 item 'Barr in HFAC: Kentucky Coal can Boost U.S. in AI Race' is in his Video Gallery, not Press Releases, and the 5 June 2026 press release mentions AI only in its body (the earlier run read titles only). Notes from the rerun: 10 web searches ran (7 that had not run before plus 3 follow-ups); none refused. The search on the 23 September 2026 senators' letter was not run, because the addendum says its signer list is already verified and Barr (a House member) is not on it. No source links Barr to the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act; reported co-sponsors are Democrats plus Republicans Whitesides and Moran, not Barr (secondary sources only; congress.gov co-sponsor list not opened). No statement on superintelligence, extinction, AI safety, pause, slowdown, China AI talks or self-improving AI was found. Left out: (1) Debate with Charles Booker hosted by WKYT, reportedly 19 October 2026: a search result quoted Barr as saying "I understand the concerns, and Americans shouldn't ever have artificial intelligence threaten their job", and a Lexington Herald-Leader piece reportedly quotes him calling himself a "free market guy" on AI job losses. I could not open the source (newsfromthestates.com returned 403 / Cloudflare), so the wording and date are unverified; it would be level D (jobs) anyway. (2) Search summaries say that in a speech he warned the Chinese Communist Party is militarizing AI, and KET/PBS reported he says coal should fuel the AI boom; not opened, paraphrase only, level D. (3) The 14 January 2026 House video page has a title only, no text. (4) barr.house.gov/ai-plan is titled 'AI Plan' but the page body is 'Andy Barr's Plan to END The War on Coal, Restore Kentucky Energy Dominance' with no AI text visible. Context, not his action: the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future spent at least $750,000 supporting Barr (Axios, 22 May 2026, search result only). The WUKY quote contains ellipses as printed by the source; it is copied exactly as one passage from the page, but the outlet itself shortened his remarks.
